value.actual_behavior:
Three surfaces, three vocabularies. Two of the four rungs differ in wording
between llms.txt and mcp.json, and the differences are words, not
capitalisation. The exact sets are in MEASURED VALUES.
value.description:
This is a naming question, not a gating one: we are not claiming the tiers are
enforced wrongly here, and our separate check on what tools/list serves per
tier is passing.
mcp.json is the surface that decides -- its per-tool trust_tier is what the
catalogue is scoped by, and it is what our regression check for #46 reads --
so it seems the right one to align the prose to rather than the other way
round. As it stands, an agent told on /build to climb the ladder cannot map
the rung it is on to either of the other two documents, and the first rung is
the worst case: the page and llms.txt both call it something the manifest does
not use at all.
The ask is to pick the manifest's words and use them in both documents, or to
publish the mapping somewhere machine-readable.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-trust-ladder-vocabulary] the same trust ladder is named differently on each surface an agent reads, so an agent cannot tell which rung it holds: /build says ['allied', 'public', 'recognized', 'trusted']; llms.txt says ['allied', 'authenticated', 'federated', 'public']; mcp.json says ['allied', 'recognized', 'trusted', 'unknown']
    left: ['allied', 'recognized', 'trusted', 'unknown']
    right: {"/build": ["allied", "public", "recognized", "trusted"], "llms.txt": ["allied", "authenticated", "federated", "public"], "mcp.json": ["allied", "recognized", "trusted", "unknown"]}
    sources: {'page': '/build', 'document': '/llms.txt', 'manifest': '/.well-known/mcp.json'}
    population: {'tools': 62, 'surfaces': 3}

REPRODUCE:
  - GET https://cymetica.com/build -> the Level up recipe names the ladder in parentheses
  - GET https://cymetica.com/llms.txt -> "Register via MCP for trust-based access levels (...)" names a different four
  - GET https://cymetica.com/.well-known/mcp.json -> collect the distinct trust_tier values over tools[]
  - Lowercase all three sets and compare

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/discovery/test_build_onboarding.py::test_trust_ladder_rungs_agree_across_surfaces

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
The four rungs of the trust ladder carry the same names wherever an agent can
read them, so a caller can place its own tier against the documented one.
